title: Hebbian fast-weight Mirror basis
hypothesis: A shared basis of Hebbian fast matrices plus transient episode coordinates can preserve one-shot associative recall while reducing writable fast-state bytes and update work versus a full per-episode matrix.
mirror_coordinate: Transient coefficients over a shared fast-matrix basis

development.selection_metric: heldout key-value retrieval nRMSE, writable bytes, write MACs

success_gate: Heldout nRMSE <= 0.02; at least 25% fewer combined persistent plus writable bytes than full matrix; online write MAC <=1.25x full outer-product update; no leakage after reset.
failure_gate: Quality gate missed or savings <25% or write MAC >1.25x; native factor control matching Mirror means no Mirror-specific attribution.
boundaries: Synthetic content-addressable associative memory, no trained network claim.
Task state is freshly zeroed per episode.
Fresh seeds 31 and 53 are never used for tuning.
